headline: Norwood Park and Edison Park sit in Ward 41, Chicago's sunniest, most lake-distant ward.
summary:
Ohare, Norwood Park, Edison Park and Jefferson Park make up Ward 41, sitting in tenth place out of Chicago's fifty wards, inside the top fifth of the field. Its strongest numbers are physical. Ground-level spots here get more direct sunlight across the year than anywhere else in Chicago, true on the summer solstice and the winter one alike. The ward also logs the fewest abandoned-vehicle and bike-lane parking complaints per square kilometer anywhere in the city, and its reported violent crime rate comes in lowest on this data set.

The softer numbers trace back to distance. A modeled estimate of how often adults spend an evening with friends weekly puts Ward 41 last of the fifty, and public transit use for commuting lands 49th. Divvy ridership and straight-line distance from the lake round out the bottom of the list too. Ward 41 sits at the city's far edge, away from downtown and the lakefront, which explains a good share of those softer numbers.
reading_the_rankings: Start with the violent crime number, where Ward 41 comes in lowest of the fifty. That figure leans on a stand-in for population. Crime counts get split across ward lines by each census tract's land area, not by where people actually live inside it, so a tract that straddles two wards can hand some of a neighbor's crime total to Ward 41's side of the ledger, or the reverse. The last-place rank on seeing friends weekly is softer still. It is not a headcount. It borrows its behavior pattern from a national sample of adults who share Ward 41's rough demographic profile, and the group behind it grades the result low confidence on its own scale. The bottom rank on Divvy rides has the opposite shape. Count down twenty-seven wards from Ward 41 on this measure, and the score has still not dropped two points, because a full eleven points of spread holds half of the wards in this measure. Last place sits inside a thick cluster rather than standing apart from it.

news.headline: After 4 Deaths At Norwood Park Metra Crossing, Safety Improvements Underway
news.note: Union Pacific began installing a four-quadrant gate system at the Nagle Avenue Metra crossing in Norwood Park, the site of four deaths and 12 collisions since 2010.
